newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Burns Philp hires U.S. businessman as new boss.
newsitem.headline: Burns Philp hires U.S. businessman as new boss.

text.p: Food ingredients group Burns Philp and Co Ltd said on Friday that it had appointed U.S. businessman Tom Degnan as managing director and chief executive officer to replace Ian Clack from September 1.
Degnan was formerly group vice president at Milwaukee-based Universal Foods Corp with responsibility for the yeast, dehydrated foods, and Asia Pacific divisions.

"Mr Degnan's well-regarded skills as a manager, his excellent record, and his detailed knowledge of the yeast industry worldwide make him an ideal CEO for Burns Philp," Burns Philp chairman Alan McGregor said.
He said Degnan was respected by company managers as a competitor, particularly for his focus on profits.

"He is widely respected in the yeast/bakery industry in the U.S.A. and elsewhere and is well known for his extensive knowledge of the yeast industry which will be our core business in the future," McGregor said.
"He is well placed to manage the existing business and to pursue the numerous growth opportunities for the company in yeast and related areas."

The company said on May 19 that it would sell its herb and spice businesses, which are focussed on the United States and European markets, after years of various restructurings which failed to achieve adequate returns.
Analysts have valued the operations at about A$600 million (US$444 million).

The company has been regarded as a potential takeover target for the lasst few months, especially since New Zealand-based businessman Graeme Hart acquired a 15 percent stake and with the company's settlement of its Estate Mortgage legal case for a payment of A$116.4 million.

Its shares, which languished below A$2.00 before the restructuring announcement, has since risen to around the A$2.50 level paid by Hart in his on-market spending spree which surprised fund managers and analysts.
Hart also has options over another four percent which would take him to the takeover threshold.
Burns Philp shares were two cents lower at A$2.49 at 1.15 p.m. (0315 GMT).
The company's announcement about the appointment of Degnan coincided with a statement from Standard and Poor's Corp that it had downgraded the company's debt ratings to BBB/A3 from BBB plus/A2.
